review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked its definitions against the rest of Mathlib: contractLeftAux, contractLeft, contractRight, changeFormAux, changeForm, changeFormEquiv and equivExterior. I grepped Mathlib for contraction and interior-product concepts. The only related hit was Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean, which is tensor-product contraction (evaluating a dual against a tensor factor). It is not the Clifford-algebra left/right contraction by a dual vector, so it can't replace these definitions. I found no existing Mathlib interior product or Clifford contraction. The file already builds on existing concepts: foldr/foldr', reverse, QuadraticMap.associated, BilinForm.toQuadraticMap, Module.Dual and ExteriorAlgebra. contractRight is defined via reverse and contractLeft, so it does not duplicate anything. changeFormEquiv is a plain LinearEquiv built from changeForm. I found no justified finding. I did not search other Mathlib directories exhaustively. Under the rubric, the exterior-algebra contraction, if it exists elsewhere, would only be a later specialisation.
